title: Death Note (2006–2007 TV Anime) Structured Question Bank
adaptationBoundary: Only the 37-episode Death Note television anime broadcast in 2006–2007 is included. Manga-only material, the Relight specials, live-action films and series, novels, games, and fan interpretations are excluded.
notes: Episode numbers and titles were cross-checked against the anime episode list and the official Nippon TV series page, which identifies 37 television episodes.
All questions use original wording and target one objectively verifiable fact from the television anime.
The Relight compilation specials are not counted as television episodes and are outside the adaptation boundary.

questions.prompt: Where does Light Yagami first find the Death Note?
questions.explanation: Light picks up the notebook on the grounds of his high school in the opening episode.

questions.prompt: Who is the shinigami that dropped the notebook Light finds?
questions.explanation: Ryuk is the shinigami who drops the Death Note into the human world and later approaches Light.

questions.prompt: What name does the public give the mysterious killer?
questions.explanation: The public adopts Kira, the Japanese rendering of 'killer,' as the name for the unknown murderer.

questions.prompt: Which region does L reveal Kira is located in through his television trap?
questions.explanation: L's broadcast is targeted to Kanto, revealing that Kira is in that region of Japan.

questions.prompt: What happens to a person whose name is written in the Death Note, assuming the notebook's conditions are met?
questions.explanation: The notebook's central rule is that a human whose name is written in it dies.

questions.prompt: What is the name of Light's father?
questions.explanation: Light's father and the police official leading the investigation is Soichiro Yagami.

questions.prompt: Which criminal is Light's first test subject after he begins using the notebook?
questions.explanation: Light first tests the notebook on Kurou Otoharada, a criminal shown on television.

questions.prompt: What type of death does Light initially use for most of his criminal targets?
questions.explanation: Light's early public pattern is a wave of apparently natural heart attacks.

questions.prompt: What is Raye Penber's occupation in the investigation?
questions.explanation: Raye Penber is an FBI agent assigned to investigate people connected to the Kira case.

questions.prompt: What does Light use to force the man following him to reveal his identity?
questions.explanation: Light engineers a bus hijacking and uses the resulting encounter to learn that his follower is Raye Penber.

questions.prompt: How many FBI agents in Japan are killed as a result of Light's train gambit?
questions.explanation: Light coerces Raye Penber into writing the names of twelve FBI agents, killing them all.

questions.prompt: Which alias does L use when he first confronts Kira on television?
questions.explanation: L uses the condemned criminal Lind L. Tailor as the bait in his first televised challenge.

questions.prompt: What does Light say he wants to become after using the notebook to remake society?
options: The god of a new world
The next head of the FBI
questions.explanation: Light repeatedly describes his intended role as the god of a new, crime-free world.

questions.prompt: What two pieces of information can shinigami eyes show above a human's head?
questions.explanation: The eyes show a human's name and lifespan, information normally unavailable to humans.

questions.prompt: Why does Light refuse Ryuk's offer of shinigami eyes?
options: The eyes would erase his memories
The deal would cost half his remaining lifespan
The eyes work only on criminals
Ryuk asks for the notebook in return
questions.explanation: The eye deal would halve Light's remaining lifespan, so he declines it.

questions.prompt: How does Light continue killing during the room-surveillance operation?
options: He hides a television inside a potato-chip bag
He memorizes every newspaper for later
He uses a second notebook supplied by L
He sends names through the police database
questions.explanation: Light conceals a portable television in a potato-chip bag and writes names while appearing to snack.

questions.prompt: At which institution do Light and L first meet face to face?
questions.explanation: Light meets L at the entrance ceremony for To-Oh University.

questions.prompt: What alias does L use when he introduces himself to Light at the university?
questions.explanation: L presents himself as Hideki Ryuga, borrowing the name of a famous idol.

questions.prompt: Which sport does L use to test Light's behavior and reasoning?
questions.explanation: L challenges Light to a tennis match and discusses the Kira case during it.

questions.prompt: What medical emergency briefly takes Soichiro Yagami out of the investigation?
questions.explanation: Soichiro suffers a heart attack after L's tennis match with Light and is taken to hospital.

questions.prompt: Which television station receives the mysterious tapes associated with the second Kira?
questions.explanation: The prerecorded messages are sent to Sakura TV, which begins broadcasting them.

questions.prompt: Which member of the investigation team dies outside Sakura TV?
questions.explanation: Hirokazu Ukita dies at Sakura TV after going to stop the broadcasts.

questions.prompt: Which shinigami is attached to Misa Amane when she contacts the Kira case?
questions.explanation: Rem accompanies Misa and is the shinigami who gives her the second notebook context in the anime.

questions.prompt: What special ability has Misa obtained by the time she approaches Kira?
options: The ability to see the future
questions.explanation: Misa has made the shinigami-eye deal, allowing her to see names and lifespans.

questions.prompt: Where does the task force send Matsuda and Light to look for the second Kira?
questions.explanation: The team investigates Aoyama on the date given in the second Kira's message.

questions.prompt: Why can Misa identify Light as Kira when she sees him?
options: His lifespan is printed on his school uniform
A Death Note owner's lifespan is invisible to her eyes
questions.explanation: Misa cannot see a Death Note owner's lifespan, and that absence identifies Light to her.

questions.prompt: What does Misa do instead of accepting the police offer to reduce the second Kira's punishment?
options: She goes to find and introduce herself to Light
questions.explanation: Misa ignores the offer and seeks out the real Kira, whom she recognizes as Light.

questions.prompt: What conclusion does L draw from the Sakura TV tapes?
options: They are from Kira's first notebook
They likely come from a different Kira
They are fabricated by the FBI
questions.explanation: The tapes use a different method and voice, leading L to suspect a second Kira.

questions.prompt: How does Soichiro enter Sakura TV's building to seize the tapes?
options: He disguises himself as a reporter
He hijacks a bus and crashes into the lobby
He walks in with a television crew
questions.explanation: Soichiro drives a hijacked bus into the lobby so the police can seize the tapes without exposing their faces.

questions.prompt: What does Light arrange around himself at Aoyama to conceal Misa's view of his face?
questions.explanation: Light has friends surround him so the shinigami following Misa cannot easily identify the real Kira.

questions.prompt: What does Misa do with ownership of her Death Note after being detained?
options: She buries it under Sakura TV
questions.explanation: Misa gives up ownership, causing her memories connected to the notebook to disappear.

questions.prompt: What does Light do as part of his plan to make himself appear innocent?
options: He relinquishes ownership of his Death Note
questions.explanation: Light relinquishes ownership and arranges confinement so he will forget being Kira.

questions.prompt: Where does Light spend part of the confinement plan?
questions.explanation: Light asks to be confined in a cell without television as part of the innocence test.

questions.prompt: What happens to the killings while Light and Misa are confined?
options: They continue, weakening the case against Light and Misa
questions.explanation: Kira killings continue during the confinement, making Light's apparent innocence more plausible.

questions.prompt: What unusual arrangement does L impose after Light joins the active investigation?
questions.explanation: L has himself physically chained to Light so the two can be observed together.

questions.prompt: Which investigator leaves the task force during the early Yotsuba investigation?
questions.explanation: Aizawa leaves the group after disagreements over the risks and L's methods.

questions.prompt: Which pair of independent operatives does L bring into the Yotsuba investigation?
questions.explanation: L recruits the thief Wedy and con man Aiber to support the investigation.

questions.prompt: Which organization is linked to the corporate killings in the Yotsuba investigation?
questions.explanation: The murders are traced to executives within Yotsuba Group.

questions.prompt: What cover identity does Matsuda use while investigating Yotsuba?
questions.explanation: Matsuda enters Yotsuba while pretending to be Misa's manager.

questions.prompt: Who infiltrates Yotsuba on the task force's behalf to gather information?
questions.explanation: L asks Misa to use her entertainment connection to infiltrate Yotsuba and learn more.

questions.prompt: Who is identified as the third Kira during the Yotsuba arc?
questions.explanation: Misa's recovered memories point to Kyosuke Higuchi as the active Yotsuba Kira.

questions.prompt: What additional deal does Higuchi make when he is cornered?
options: A deal to become a shinigami
A deal to erase the Death Note
A deal to trade places with L
questions.explanation: Higuchi accepts the shinigami-eye deal during the trap and chase.

questions.prompt: What happens to Higuchi at the end of the pursuit?
options: He escapes to the United States
He is arrested by the task force
questions.explanation: The task force captures Higuchi, allowing the notebook and its rules to be examined.

questions.prompt: What do the investigators encounter for the first time after Higuchi's arrest?
options: A Death Note and the rules written in it
questions.explanation: The task force physically encounters the Death Note and begins examining its written rules.

questions.prompt: Whom does Rem kill at the end of the first major investigation?
questions.explanation: Rem kills both L and Watari to protect Misa, producing the investigation's decisive catastrophe.

questions.prompt: What is the title of episode 26, the transition episode after L's death?
questions.explanation: Episode 26 is titled Renewal and functions as a recap and transition into the successor storyline.

questions.prompt: What new professional position does Light officially take five years later?
questions.explanation: The timeskip shows Light joining the National Police Agency as an investigator.

questions.prompt: What does SPK stand for in the successor investigation?
questions.explanation: Near forms the Special Provision for Kira, abbreviated SPK.

questions.prompt: With whom does Mello ally himself after leaving Wammy's House?
questions.explanation: Mello works with criminals and uses that alliance to pursue the notebook and Kira.

questions.prompt: Which member of the Yagami family is kidnapped to obtain the notebook?
questions.explanation: Mello's group kidnaps Sayu Yagami and demands the Death Note in exchange.

questions.prompt: Why does Sidoh enter the human world during Mello's storyline?
options: He is searching for his stolen notebook
questions.explanation: Sidoh comes to the human world looking for the Death Note that Mello possesses.

questions.prompt: What does Soichiro do to obtain Mello's real name during the raid?
options: He asks Ryuk to write it
He reads it from Near's files
questions.explanation: Soichiro trades half his remaining lifespan for shinigami eyes so he can see Mello's name.

questions.prompt: What public stance does the United States announce in episode 30?
questions.explanation: The United States declares neutrality rather than openly supporting either side.

questions.prompt: What does Mello reveal to Near about the Death Note?
options: That the notebook cannot kill criminals
questions.explanation: Mello tells Near that the Death Note contains fake rules, including the 13-day rule used as a defense.

questions.prompt: Which former task-force member gives Near information after meeting him?
questions.explanation: Aizawa meets Near and supplies information about the Japanese investigation.

questions.prompt: Who becomes Light's selected new second Kira and public spokesperson?
questions.explanation: Light selects Kiyomi Takada to act as the new Kira spokesperson.

questions.prompt: Which prosecutor does Light choose to act as the new Kira?
questions.explanation: Light chooses Teru Mikami as the new Kira and directs him through Takada.

questions.prompt: What does Near's group do before the final phase of the confrontation?
options: The SPK gives Light the notebook
questions.explanation: Near and the SPK travel to Japan as the final investigation moves there.

questions.prompt: Who tails Mikami and helps expose the notebook's location?
questions.explanation: Gevanni follows Mikami and photographs the notebook, giving Near evidence for the substitution plan.

questions.prompt: What is the title of episode 36, the episode immediately before the finale?
questions.explanation: Episode 36 is titled 1.28, referring to the date of the final confrontation.

questions.prompt: At which warehouse does the final confrontation take place?
questions.explanation: Near arranges the final meeting at the Yellow Box Warehouse.

questions.prompt: What does Mikami write in the notebook during the final warehouse test?
options: The names of the task-force members only
questions.explanation: Mikami writes the names of everyone present except Light, following Light's instruction.

questions.prompt: What does the group observe after the supposed notebook names are written at the warehouse?
options: No one dies after forty seconds
questions.explanation: The expected deaths do not occur after forty seconds, exposing the notebook substitution.

questions.prompt: Who writes Light Yagami's name in a Death Note at the end of the anime?
questions.explanation: Ryuk writes Light's name in his own Death Note after telling Light that the promise has come due.

questions.prompt: What is the immediate cause of Light's death after Ryuk writes his name?
questions.explanation: Light dies from the notebook's specified default death: a heart attack.

questions.prompt: Which investigator shoots Light during the final confrontation?
questions.explanation: Matsuda shoots Light after Light attempts to use a hidden piece of the notebook.

questions.prompt: Where has Light concealed the notebook fragment he tries to use at the warehouse?
questions.explanation: Light keeps a torn notebook piece in his watch for a last attempt to write a name.

questions.prompt: What does Mikami use to make the final hidden notebook accessible before the warehouse meeting?
questions.explanation: Mikami retrieves the real notebook from a safety-deposit box, a move that lets Gevanni track it.

questions.prompt: Who is killed during Mello's operation involving Takada?
questions.explanation: Mello dies after carrying out the abduction that disrupts Light and Near's plans.

questions.prompt: Which character's kidnapping causes Mikami to act outside Light's intended schedule?
questions.explanation: Takada's kidnapping prompts Mikami to access the real notebook, revealing its location.

questions.prompt: What does Near's team substitute before the warehouse meeting?
options: A fake notebook for the real one
questions.explanation: Near's team replaces the real notebook with a replica so Mikami's writing will fail.

questions.prompt: What is Near's given name?
questions.explanation: Near's real name is Nate River, one of the successor details exposed in the endgame.

questions.prompt: Which title is used for the anime's final episode?
questions.explanation: The 37th and final episode is titled New World.

questions.prompt: Which title belongs to the episode in which L and Watari die?
questions.explanation: Episode 25, Silence, contains Rem's fatal intervention that kills L and Watari.

questions.prompt: How many numbered television episodes make up the 2006–2007 anime series?
questions.explanation: Nippon TV identifies the animated series as 37 episodes; the two Relight specials are separate works and are excluded here.
